title: Binding validation: tolerate runtime-managed extra agent entries in model-selections
refined_problem: Diagnosed with a deterministic one-liner diff: model-selections.json contains an extra 'verifier' agent entry that the OpenCode runtime persists (its own multi-task agent-model state), while the active binding for MVP-EVAL-001 records only its own 6 routed agents. validate_provider_active compares the whole lists, so the runtime's extra entry fails the semantic equality and deadlocks receipt_review.prepare. The binding is the authority for its own task's agents; entries for agents outside the binding belong to the runtime's cross-task state and must not invalidate it.

original_request.text: diagnostic output: ACTIVE agents [debugger, explorer, implementer, planner, reviewer, test-designer] vs FILE agents [same + verifier]; DIFF AGENT: verifier; file task_id MVP-EVAL-001 schema 2

target_users: Harness operators with live OpenCode sessions
outcomes: validate_provider_active accepts a model-selections file whose EXTRA agent entries (agents not present in the binding) belong to the runtime, while still rejecting any modification of the binding's own agent entries
success_metrics: New regression tests: extra-agent file accepted; bound-agent mutation with extra-agent file rejected

in: scripts/harnesslib.py guarded-raise branch: compare per-agent (agent-keyed dicts) filtered to the binding's own agents
backend/tests/test_binding_drift.py: extend with T4 (extra verifier entry accepted) and T5 (extra entry + bound-agent mutation rejected)
out: Removal of the runtime's own file ownership (structural redesign, backlog)

mvp.goal: Unblock MVP-EVAL-001 closure without weakening tamper detection over the binding's own agents.
includes: Per-agent comparison filtered to binding agents
excludes: Structural redesign of the dual-writer path

assumptions: The binding's own agent entries are the tamper surface; extra runtime entries are cross-task state
An attacker able to write the file can also rewrite active-task.json (same trust domain), so per-agent comparison does not materially weaken integrity
challenges: Keep the comparison strict for bound agents: any field mutation must reject
